newsitem.title: JAPAN: Eisai gets FDA approval for Alzheimer's drug.
newsitem.headline: Eisai gets FDA approval for Alzheimer's drug.

text.p: Eisai Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it had received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for its Alzheimer's drug Aricept.
Eisai said in a statement that its U.S. subsidiary, Eisai America Inc, received approval for the new drug in the United States on Monday.
Aricept is a drug for mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease, the company said.
Another Eisai unit in the United States would start selling the drug there in January 1997, an Eisai spokesman said.
Pfizer Inc, which agreed a tie-up with Eisai on sales of Aricept and the development of new drugs for Alzheimer's disease in 1994, would co-promote the drug in the United States, the spokesman said.
Profit would be divided between Eisai's sales unit and Pfizer, he said.
In Japan, Eisai started the final phase of clinical tests of the drug in August and was likely to apply for new drug approval from Japan's Health Ministry in 1999, the spokesman said.
